title: Security appliances software versions MX 26.2.2 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Beta MX Security & SD-WAN firmware is now available

Executive summary: MX 26.2.2 is the second beta release for the MX 26.2 release family.
This release adds custom intrusion policies, WAN Uplink Sharing, and organization-wide port profiles.
It also expands routing, firewall, and cellular management capabilities, including MP-BGP, ECMP, and a second wired WAN uplink for Z4 and Z4C appliances.
Additional fixes address VPN, routing, traffic inspection, and connectivity.
What's new: Introduced custom intrusion policies, allowing administrators to create policies by overriding rules or rule groups from a base policy.
Added WAN Uplink Sharing for warm spare deployments, allowing an MX high-availability pair to use WAN circuits connected to either appliance.
Introduced organization-wide port profiles and an MX Ports tab for creating reusable configurations and statically applying them to eligible MX LAN ports.
Added MP-BGP support for exchanging IPv4 and IPv6 routes over a single iBGP session between AutoVPN peers.
Added ECMP for eBGP routes learned over multiple IPsec VPN tunnels, distributing new flows across equal-cost paths.
Enabled Port 2 on Z4 and Z4C appliances to be converted from a LAN port to a second wired WAN uplink.
Added support for configuring cellular data management profiles.
Introduced Local Status Page support for viewing SIM status and managing SIM card PIN codes.
Expanded API support for cellular geolocation, serving-cell information, and cellular band selection.
Expanded organization-wide group policy rules with FQDN destinations and support for selecting Secure Group Tags as destinations in inbound VPN firewall rules for AutoVPN traffic.
Bug fixes - general fixes: Resolved an issue that could prevent IKEv1 Client VPN connections from establishing when IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks was enabled. (MX-50879)
Fixed an issue that could prevent Cisco Secure Client VPN connections over reduced-MTU paths when upstream networks blocked fragmented packets. (MX-23697)
Corrected an issue that could prevent peer-initiated IPsec or Cisco Secure Client VPN connections from reaching an MX appliance when No-NAT was enabled on the receiving uplink. (MX-49686)
Resolved an issue that could prevent SD-WAN statistics from populating and policies from applying after an AutoVPN contact port changed on a passthrough-mode appliance. (MX-44815)
Corrected an issue that could drop AutoVPN traffic when a downstream peer connected through an upstream MX LAN subnet that was not enabled for VPN. (MX-50550)
Corrected an issue that could cause Dashboard to display an empty next hop for routes learned from link-local IPv6 eBGP peers. (MX-49629)
Fixed a rare issue that could leave the routing service stuck while starting. (MX-49953)
Resolved an issue that could prevent an eBGP-learned default route from being advertised to AutoVPN spokes when the route was learned in an additional VRF. (MX-50834)
Fixed an issue that could prevent AutoVPN-learned routes from being advertised to a transit-enabled eBGP peer in an additional VRF. (MX-51009)
Corrected an issue that could incorrectly apply content filtering to internal and appliance-management IPv6 traffic. (MX-46104)
Resolved an issue that could allow traffic to FQDNs removed from organization-wide group policy firewall rules until cached DNS entries expired. (MX-49341)
Corrected an issue that could cause AMP cloud lookup errors to be reported in syslog as malicious file events when fail-close behavior blocked the download. (MX-46715)
Resolved an issue that could reset HTTPS connections when TLS inspection was enabled and application classification changed during the connection. (MX-50685)
Resolved an issue that could cause memory-constrained MX appliances with many connected LAN ports to restart unexpectedly after LAN-side topology changes. (MX-51105)
Bug fixes - limited platform fixes: Resolved an issue that could cause Azure vMX instances with Accelerated Networking to restart unexpectedly when switching between routed and passthrough modes. (MX-49700)
Corrected an issue that could leave 1 Gbps copper SFP ports without link after startup on C8355-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-49859)
Fixed an issue that could cause cellular connectivity to become unavailable or unstable on MX67C appliances after upgrading to MX 26.2. (MX-49983)
Improved HTTPS inspection throughput on supported devices when intrusion detection and prevention was enabled. (MX-49653)
Corrected an issue that could prevent vMX appliances from downloading intrusion detection and prevention rules after startup. (MX-51218)
Improved HTTPS inspection behavior on high-capacity MX appliances when the concurrent-flow limit was reached. (MX-50149)
Legacy products notice: When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.
When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.
Known issues: On MX95 and MX105 appliances, 1 Gbps fiber links may not establish when the connected device uses auto-negotiation. (MX-51846)
Client VPN connections may fail when upstream NAT changes the client's IKE source port from UDP 500. (MX-51712)
On MX appliances in HA with a virtual IP, enabling multiple uplinks for a Non-Meraki VPN peer may prevent all Non-Meraki VPN tunnels from establishing. (MX-49849)
Dashboard may display only one next hop for BGP routes using ECMP, although traffic continues to use all equal-cost paths. (MX-50932)
Certain custom intrusion prevention rules may prevent WAN Uplink Sharing from establishing shared uplinks. (MX-51442)
In some WAN Uplink Sharing deployments, iBGP sessions may remain down after uplink sharing is enabled even though AutoVPN is established. (MX-50729)
In WAN Uplink Sharing deployments where shared WAN interfaces use overlapping subnets, eBGP sessions on a shared uplink may repeatedly disconnect and reconnect. (MX-51229)
Other: Added the cellular IP address to the Local Status Page.
The product complies with EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2: 2024
